items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1962-01-31
items.q: he went away the same time Bunk went away. Bunk Johnson.

ctx.x: I don't know what happened to him.

He went away from here. Long time ago. I think he died. He went, he went, he went, uh, he went away the same time Bunk went away. Bunk Johnson. When Bunk left here, Prevost left. And they went up the line somewhere in different places and stayed away a long time, you see.

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: Bunk, uh, I played in a band that he played in

ctx.x: Well, I was gonna ask about some more of the old time trumpet players. You talked about Joe Oliver and Kepard a little. I remember Bunk. Did you ever play with Trump Johnson?

Bunk? Bunk, uh, I played in a band that he played in, but I never did, uh, because he played in, you know, he was a trumpet player that he'd come around and play, say, like, uh, at Fruit Close, at, at, at, at Harry Parker. At, uh, uh, Huntson Nagel, Billy Phillips. He'd come, the fellas would hire him on a job, see? And them trumpet players.

couldn't just naturally keep up, you know, playing all the week, you know, like that. They get tired and want to take a little, you know, time off from the night, you know. And he'd send Bunkie in his place, you know, like one of those fellas would lay off and send him in his place. Well, that's how he, well, he only went, he got his band, he just went off, you see, when he went away from here, I think he went, I don't remember him having no band of himself.

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1959-08-11
items.q: Bunk Johnson was playing with the Silver Leaf, I think.

ctx.x: Did they have some of the blowing instruments too or mostly strings?

They had blowing instruments too, yeah. Oh, the dance band? Yeah, they had, I think Bunk Johnson was playing in one of the bands at that time. Remember Bunk Johnson? Bunk Johnson was playing with the Silver Leaf, I think. Well, I played with the Silver Leaf for a good while. There's spot jobs, you know, up on the Pelican. Who was the leader of that? Uh, uh, Poisey Umphrey. Oh, Percy or was it his father? No, Poisey. Poisey, yeah. Poisey Umphrey. Willie Umphrey. Willie Umphrey. Willie Umphrey, yeah. The clarinet…
Was that the place called, um, later the Entertainers or 101 Ranch? Yeah.
